subject: Accounting
title: Transfer Pricing Internally
description: A 60-second lesson on Transfer Pricing Internally.

hook.text: Division A makes parts for Division B. What price should A charge? Too high or low distorts both.

buildup.text: Transfer pricing sets the cost of goods or services exchanged between divisions of the same company.

discovery.text: Options include market price, cost-plus, or negotiated price—each has trade-offs.

twist.text: Wrong transfer prices make profitable divisions look bad and struggling ones look good—corrupting decisions.

climax.text: The goal is a price that motivates both divisions to act in the company's best interest.

punchline.text: Internal prices shape internal behavior. Get them right.

quiz.question: What is internal transfer pricing?
options: The price charged between divisions of the same company
The price charged to external customers

details.summary: Transfer pricing determines the price at which divisions within the same company buy and sell goods or services to each other. This topic explains market-based, cost-based, and negotiated transfer pricing methods and their impact on divisional performance measurement.
details.whyItMatters: The transfer price directly affects each division's reported profit. A poorly set transfer price can make one division look great while starving another, leading to dysfunctional decisions and conflicts.
takeaways: Market-based transfer prices are ideal when an external market price exists—they simulate arm's-length transactions
Cost-based prices work when no market exists but can demotivate the selling division if set at cost
The general transfer pricing rule: minimum price equals the selling division's variable cost plus opportunity cost

faq.question: What is transfer pricing?
faq.answer: Transfer pricing is the price charged when one division of a company sells goods or services to another division of the same company. It determines how total company profit is split between divisions and impacts how each division's performance is evaluated.

faq.question: What is the best transfer pricing method?
faq.answer: Market-based pricing is generally best when a competitive external market exists, as it simulates an arm's-length transaction. When no market exists, a negotiated price between the minimum (variable cost plus opportunity cost) and maximum (external market price) often works best.
